questions.question: Which engine powers the AMR26?

paragraphs: Honda RA626H, a 1.6-litre turbocharged V6 hybrid power unit. It replaced the Mercedes power unit used on the AMR25.

links.label: Aston Martin F1 — AMR25 official technical specifications

questions.question: Does the engine run entirely on electricity?

paragraphs: No. It has both a combustion engine and a powerful electric system. Aston Martin describes the 2026 power-unit concept as approximately a 50:50 combustion/electric power split, not a fully electric car.

questions.question: Does sustainable fuel mean zero tailpipe emissions?

paragraphs: No. Combustion still releases CO₂. The sustainability claim concerns qualifying renewable or non-fossil carbon sources and the fuel’s lifecycle impact, not zero exhaust CO₂. The report does not provide AMR26 tailpipe or whole-car lifecycle emissions.

questions.question: What fuel does the AMR26 use?

paragraphs: Aramco ProForce+, the FIA-compliant 100% sustainable fuel supplied to Aston Martin Aramco for the 2026 season.

questions.question: How is the fuel sustainable?

paragraphs: FIA rules require approved advanced sustainable feedstocks and greenhouse-gas standards. They can include non-food biomass, municipal waste, and qualifying renewable non-biological sources.

questions.question: What percentage less CO2 does ProForce+ produce?

paragraphs: The official car pages consulted do not disclose a verified AMR26-specific percentage lifecycle CO₂ reduction. Display “Not publicly disclosed” rather than an invented figure.

questions.question: What does 32% circularity mean?

paragraphs: The ESG report records 32% material circularity for the AMR25 using the sport’s circularity methodology, which considers material inflows and outflows across car development. It does not mean the chassis is 32% recycled carbon fibre.

links.label: Make A Mark ESG Report 2025 — AMR25 material circularity

questions.question: How much carbon fibre did Aston Martin recycle?

paragraphs: Its 2025 Make A Mark report states 1.3 tonnes of carbon fibre were recycled during 2025, an operational recycling figure.

links.label: Make A Mark ESG Report 2025 — carbon fibre recycling

questions.question: What is the AMR26 chassis recycled-content percentage?

paragraphs: A verified AMR26-specific recycled-carbon-fibre or chassis circularity figure was not found in the reviewed official sources. Mark it “Not reported.”

links.label: Make A Mark ESG Report 2025 — AMR25 material circularity

questions.question: Does the AMR26 still have DRS?

paragraphs: No conventional rear-wing-only DRS. The 2026 car uses active front and rear aero surfaces, with Corner and Straight modes. Overtaking also uses a separate electrical Overtake Mode.

questions.question: How does active aerodynamics help efficiency?

paragraphs: It reduces aerodynamic drag on designated straights, lowering the energy needed to travel at speed, while Corner Mode restores downforce for grip. No AMR26-specific carbon-saving percentage is disclosed.

questions.question: Did the wings change during 2026?

paragraphs: Yes. The team reported revised front and rear wing-related parts in its major Hungarian GP upgrade package, aimed at front-end performance and rear drag/load balance.

questions.question: Is the AMR26 floor the same as the AMR25?

paragraphs: No. The 2026 regulations replace the 2022–2025 deep Venturi tunnel approach with a flatter floor and a different diffuser arrangement.

questions.question: Why should I view the diffuser in 3D?

paragraphs: The underside is difficult to see in a top view. A 3D cutaway shows how the floor and diffuser guide airflow below and behind the car.

questions.question: What changed to the floor in 2026?

paragraphs: Aston Martin’s Hungarian GP package included revisions to the floor body, fences, edge and diffuser intended to increase floor load and support the overall aero package.

questions.question: How is braking energy recovered?

paragraphs: The MGU-K converts mechanical energy into electricity, charges the energy store and deploys it for propulsion later.

questions.question: How much electrical power can it produce?

paragraphs: The 2026 regulatory maximum is 350 kW, compared with 120 kW in the previous generation. Deployment is restricted according to FIA energy-management rules.

questions.question: Where is the MGU-H?

paragraphs: There is no MGU-H on the 2026 AMR26. It was a feature of the older-generation hybrid rules and was removed for 2026.

questions.question: Why are the sidepods shaped like this?

paragraphs: Sidepods house or feed cooling systems while shaping airflow to the floor and rear car. Aston Martin revised sidepod inlets and bodywork in its 2026 Hungarian upgrade package.

questions.question: Does more cooling always mean better performance?

paragraphs: No. Larger openings can improve cooling but may increase drag or disrupt downstream airflow. Engineers balance temperatures with aero needs.

questions.question: How much energy does the AMR26 cooling system save?

paragraphs: No verified AMR26-specific energy-saving value was found in the published sources reviewed.

questions.question: How are the brakes different from ordinary cars?

paragraphs: Front brakes are hydraulic and rear braking uses brake-by-wire to balance friction braking with regenerative energy recovery.

questions.question: How much energy can the car harvest under braking?

paragraphs: Aston Martin’s engineering overview describes up to 8.5 MJ per lap under the 2026 framework; track/session energy limits and adjustments must be applied separately. This is a rules-related limit, not a recorded AMR26 lap measurement.

questions.question: Why do brake ducts matter?

paragraphs: Brake ducts must remove heat while minimizing aerodynamic drag. They form part of the integrated cooling and aerodynamic design.

questions.question: Who makes the AMR26 gearbox?

paragraphs: Aston Martin developed the eight-speed semi-automatic gearbox and hydraulics in-house at its AMR Technology Campus; the AMR25 used a Mercedes-supplied gearbox.

links.label: Aston Martin F1 — AMR25 official technical specifications

questions.question: Why did Aston Martin develop its own gearbox?

paragraphs: In-house development gives the works team greater freedom to integrate the transmission with the Honda power unit, suspension, cooling, weight distribution and aero layout.

questions.question: Does the gearbox reduce carbon emissions?

paragraphs: The reviewed car technical sources do not quantify emissions savings caused by the new gearbox. Present its engineering advantages without claiming a measured carbon benefit.

questions.question: Why is suspension an aerodynamic part?

paragraphs: Its geometry affects ride height, tire contact and airflow near the wheels and rear bodywork.

questions.question: What is unusual about Aston Martin’s 2026 rear suspension?

paragraphs: Formula 1 technical analysis describes unusually high-mounted rear upper arms, intended to give the diffuser exit more clearance and influence airflow. This is an observed technical analysis, not a measured efficiency result.

questions.question: Was suspension upgraded in Hungary?

paragraphs: Yes. Aston Martin documented rear-suspension and rear-corner refinements associated with changes to the rear floor in its major Hungary package.

questions.question: Does Aston Martin use recycled-rubber tires?

paragraphs: The reviewed sources do not support claiming recycled rubber in the AMR26 tyres. Pirelli does document FSC-certified natural rubber in Formula 1 tyres since 2024.

links.label: Pirelli — Formula 1 tires and FSC natural rubber

questions.question: What changed in 2026 tires?

paragraphs: The 2026 rules retain 18-inch wheels but call for narrower front and rear tyres than the previous generation.

questions.question: How can tire choice impact sustainability?

paragraphs: Tyre choices influence strategy, grip and wear. Any carbon-saving claim for specific compounds or races needs tyre lifecycle data that has not been established for this prototype.

links.label: Pirelli — Formula 1 tires and FSC natural rubber

people.name: Alex

portrait.brief: Editorial illustration for University student; fictional person; no inference of sensitive traits from appearance.

people.intro: Hi, I’m Alex, a fictional composite guide to Aleto leadership programme. Choose a question to explore the real programme and its published story.

article.title: Mentoring and confidence
paragraphs: A nine-month mentoring programme connects university students with members of the team.

The detailed 2025 report describes 14 students. Survey respondents reported stronger networks (93%) and growth in leadership, confidence and presentations (90%). These are self-reported outcomes, not job-placement rates.

article.title: Engineering careers and mentorship
paragraphs: A six-month pilot linked women mentors at Arm with women mentees at AMF1.
The programme page reports that 71% of mentors and mentees were highly likely to continue the relationship. This statistic describes relationship continuation, not promotion or recruitment.

article.title: Belonging at the track
paragraphs: Racing Pride and AMF1 collaborate on inclusion, visibility and welcoming motorsport communities.
The 2025 report describes campus and trackside activities, including recognition of LGBTQ+ marshals and volunteers. It does not provide a longitudinal participation outcome for this demo.

article.title: Engineering for accessibility
paragraphs: Composite design expertise supported a bespoke para-canoe seat with Paddle UK and Darkside Canoes.
The report describes three prototypes over nine months and improvements in stability and support. No numeric performance improvement is published here.

article.title: Skills beyond the service
paragraphs: The 2024 report describes support for veterans moving into technology and motorsport.
TechVets provides skills, connections and career support. The report includes a trackside IT career story; it does not establish a placement rate for the whole programme.

article.title: A practical route into motorsport
paragraphs: The Aspiring Mechanics programme supports hands-on technical learning and routes into motorsport.
The report follows a real student’s progression through vocational levels. This is an individual published story, not evidence that every participant progresses at the same rate.

article.title: Discover the work behind the race
paragraphs: Make A Mark Day brings students into the campus for workshops and career exploration.
In 2025, 257 students attended across two days, with 14 schools and community groups represented. A separate initial survey found 68% were unclear about skills needed for AI work.

article.title: Learning through real projects
paragraphs: Aramco-sponsored engineering students contributed to sustainability projects during a summer placement.

The 2025 internship page describes eight students. Work included the circularity metric project alongside career-readiness workshops. Circularity measures belong to the AMR25 methodology, not an individual intern’s personal impact.

The report describes engagement with more than 600 students from 35 countries. Reaching more than 100,000 students over three years is an ambition, not a completed outcome.
